Journal article.definition: A written composition on a topic of interest, which forms a separate part of a journal.

Dataset.definition: Data encoded in a defined structure.

Software.definition: A computer program other than a computational notebook, in either source code (text) or compiled form. Use this type for general software components supporting scholarly research. Use the “ComputationalNotebook” value for virtual notebooks.

Publication.definition: A resource consisting primarily of words for reading that is not covered by any other textual resource type in this list. (DataCite resourceTypeGeneral Text)

Preprint.definition: A version of a scholarly or scientific paper that precedes formal peer review and publication in a peer-reviewed scholarly or scientific journal.

Conference paper.definition: Article that is written with the goal of being accepted to a conference.

Presentation.definition: A set of slides containing text, tables or figures, designed to communicate ideas or research results, for viewing by an audience at a conference, symposium, seminar, lecture, workshop or other event.

Report.definition: A document that presents information in an organized format for a specific audience and purpose.

Book.definition: A medium for recording information in the form of writing or images, typically composed of many pages bound together and protected by a cover.

Other (publication).definition: A publication (textual resource) that is not covered by any other publication subtype.

Book chapter.definition: One of the main divisions of a book.

Taxonomic treatment.definition: A resource consisting primarily of words for reading that is not covered by any other textual resource type in this list. (DataCite resourceTypeGeneral Text; resourceType "Taxonomic treatment")

Figure.definition: A visual representation other than text. (DataCite resourceTypeGeneral Image; resourceType "Figure")

Journal.definition: A scholarly publication consisting of articles that is published regularly throughout the year.

Other.definition: A resource that is not covered by any other resource type in the vocabulary.

Poster.definition: A display poster, typically containing text with illustrative figures and/or tables, usually reporting research results or proposing hypotheses, submitted for acceptance to and/or presented at a conference, seminar, symposium, workshop or similar event.

Conference proceeding.definition: Collection of academic papers published in the context of an academic conference.

Thesis.definition: A written essay, treatise, or thesis, especially one written by a candidate for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy. (DataCite resourceTypeGeneral Dissertation)

Model.definition: An abstract, conceptual, graphical, mathematical or visualization model that represents empirical objects, phenomena, or physical processes.

Working paper.definition: A resource consisting primarily of words for reading that is not covered by any other textual resource type in this list. (DataCite resourceTypeGeneral Text; resourceType "Working paper")

source.query: created:[D+6h*k TO D+6h*(k+1)} AND publication_date:[2026-06-01 TO 2026-09-26], sort=oldest, size=25, page=1, four 6h slots per day, 2026-06-01..2026-09-26

labels_source: official: Zenodo/InvenioRDM resource-type vocabulary titles (live API vocabulary); definitions from DataCite Metadata Schema 4.7 resourceTypeGeneral descriptions

author_written_definitions.Other (publication): A publication (textual resource) that is not covered by any other publication subtype.
author_written_definitions.Other: A resource that is not covered by any other resource type in the vocabulary.

notes: Duplicate vocabulary title 'Other' is disambiguated by parent type, e.g. 'Other (publication)'.

Where DataCite 4.7 has a general type matching the Zenodo title (e.g. Poster, Presentation), its definition is used; otherwise the definition of Zenodo's mapped datacite_general, with the mapping noted in the card.
Wrong asked labels are never a parent/child of the gold in the vocabulary (e.g. 'Publication' vs 'Journal article') nor another image subtype when the gold is an image type, since both could apply.
States: 'Title: ...\n\nDescription: ...', HTML stripped, source text only; trimmed at a sentence boundary with ' ...' only if above 6,000 chars.
Labels are uploader-chosen on Zenodo, so some gold labels are noisy (e.g. Preprint vs Journal article, a paper filed as Poster).

Only record metadata (title, description) is used; Zenodo licenses all metadata CC0. The record's own content licence (files) varies and is kept in meta.record_content_licence; a few are NC/ND, which does not apply to the metadata text.
Snapshot: unauthenticated API caps page size at 25, so the pool is 25 records x 4 six-hour created slots x 118 days (11,800 records), the oldest in each slot; not a uniform random sample of Zenodo.
Extra cleaning beyond the spec: exact/normalised duplicate descriptions dropped (section 8 dedup).

Track F: only first versions of a Zenodo concept (metadata.relations.version index 0) are kept. Later versions can carry text first published before 2026-06-01 (verification found 10 such rows in the first build, concepts dating back to 2024-2026-05), so they are dropped.
Instructions are one fixed template with the asked label filled in.
